target_customer: Consumers (smartphone owners sharing location with friends); later businesses via a white label offer
problem: Friends and family had no battery-efficient way to see where each other were in real time without manual check-ins or opt-in invites.
business_model: Free consumer app with no disclosed revenue; later a white label location offers product for businesses

founders.name: Geoffrey Woo
founders.background_notes: YC page lists later ventures (Anti Fund, H.V.M.N., Archive); no prior employers or education given.

founders.name: Jono Chang
founders.background_notes: No bio on the YC page.

founders.name: Jon Zhang
founders.background_notes: No bio on the YC page.

competitors.name: Google Latitude
competitors.what: Location sharing between friends on Google accounts

competitors.name: Apple Find My Friends
competitors.what: Opt-in friend location sharing on iPhone, announced October 2011

competitors.name: Foursquare
competitors.traction_then: about 15 million users at end of 2011

technical_complexity.rationale: Always-on background location with low battery drain on iOS and Android and Facebook graph integration; the company claimed roughly 0.5 percent battery per hour, a hard part for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Location sharing could be copied by platform owners, and the value depended on friends joining, with Facebook login as the only graph.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apple shipped Find My Friends in 2011 and Google had Latitude; Glassmap itself was bought by Groupon in January 2013 and the app closed on February 15, 2013.

market_need_then: Location sharing was a hot 2011 and 2012 category, shown by Foursquare scale and Apple entering with Find My Friends; battery drain from constant tracking was a known complaint.

branding.domain_note: The YC listed website was ansibletechnologies.com, the owning entity per CB Insights; the glassmap domain history was not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Launch copy pitched a simple, beautiful way to show friends where you are.

brand_strength.rationale: No evidence of press about the brand itself or community; the app was shut down about a month after the acquisition.

pivots.to: White label location offers platform for businesses
pivots.why: Not stated by the source headline; TechCrunch reported the white label launch.

outcome_analysis: Glassmap launched publicly in February 2012 as a battery efficient Facebook based location sharing app in a crowded space where Apple and Google already offered similar features. It added photos and events and a white label offers product in 2012 but did not reach scale, and Groupon bought it in January 2013 apparently for the team and technology, then closed the app on February 15, 2013. No price or funding figure is public, so the exit is best read as a soft landing.
notes: Company website ansibletechnologies.com returned HTTP 503 on fetch. CB Insights lists about 20K raised and Seedtable lists an August 2011 seed with no amount; both are aggregators, so no round is recorded. Shutdown date of February 15, 2013 comes from a search summary of launch coverage. Acquisition price undisclosed.
